title: NIS 2024 · Paper 2: Solution design
instructions:
Answer all questions.
The number of marks is given in brackets [ ] at the end of each question or part question.
You should show all your work.
You can write any code in pseudocode or any other programming language that you studied.

questions.title: Documentation and data collection
questions.text: When developing a new computerised system, a software developer should write technical documentation with details of the system and a user guide.

parts.title: Documentation and data collection (a)
parts.text: Give two items that need to be included in the user guide.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Installation instructions / the steps required to install the product (1)

Details of backup procedures (1)

Required hardware and software (1)

Detailed description of the use of the full system / a step-by-step guide of how the system can perform (1)

Samples of error messages (1)

error recovery procedures- / step-by-step guide or explanation of how to fix the error (1)

[max 2]

points.criterion: Installation instructions / the steps required to install the product
Detailed description of the use of the full system / a step-by-step guide of how the system can perform
error recovery procedures- / step-by-step guide or explanation of how to fix the error

scheme.model_answer:
1. Installation instructions / the steps required to install the product.
2. Details of backup procedures.
scheme.ai_instructions: Award any two distinct items from the mark scheme, maximum 2 marks.

parts.title: Documentation and data collection (b)
parts.text: Name two benefits of using a waterfall model of the software development lifecycle (SDLC).

scheme.mark_scheme:
Uses clear structure (1)

Never moving forward until the previous phase has been completed. (1)

Highly structured with well-defined goals and timelines (1)

Encourages documentation (1)

Projects and progress are easily understood from the outside (1)

Well-suited to projects using established technologies/standard requirements (1)

When compared with other methodologies, Waterfall focuses most on a clear, defined set of steps. (1)

Determining the end goal early (1)

[max 2]

points.criterion: Never moving forward until the previous phase has been completed.
Highly structured with well-defined goals and timelines
Projects and progress are easily understood from the outside
Well-suited to projects using established technologies/standard requirements
When compared with other methodologies, Waterfall focuses most on a clear, defined set of steps.

scheme.model_answer:
1. Uses clear structure.
2. Encourages documentation.
scheme.ai_instructions: Award any two distinct benefits from the mark scheme, maximum 2 marks.

parts.title: Documentation and data collection (c)
parts.text: State two disadvantages of using questionnaires and two disadvantages of using interviews when collecting data.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Disadvantages of a questionnaire:

Limited Depth of Responses / challenging to capture complex thoughts, emotions, or subjective experiences through closed-ended questions. (1)

Low Response Rates and Non-response Bias / may not be representative of the entire population leading to inaccurate results. (1)

Disadvantages of Interviews:

Time and Resource Intensive / difficult to cover a large sample size or… (1)
… geographically dispersed participants. (1)

Potential for Interviewer Bias / Interviewers may unintentionally influence the responses (1)

[max 4]

Accept other reasonable answers

points.criterion: Questionnaire disadvantage: Limited Depth of Responses / challenging to capture complex thoughts, emotions, or subjective experiences through closed-ended questions.
Questionnaire disadvantage: Low Response Rates and Non-response Bias / may not be representative of the entire population leading to inaccurate results.
Interview disadvantage: Time and Resource Intensive / difficult to cover a large sample size or geographically dispersed participants.
Interview disadvantage: Potential for Interviewer Bias / Interviewers may unintentionally influence the responses.

scheme.model_answer:
Questionnaire: disadvantage 1: Limited depth of responses.
Questionnaire: disadvantage 2: Low response rates and non-response bias.
Interview: disadvantage 1: Time and resource intensive.
Interview: disadvantage 2: Potential for interviewer bias.
scheme.ai_instructions: Accept other reasonable disadvantages. Award up to two questionnaire disadvantages and up to two interview disadvantages, maximum 4 marks.

questions.title: System requirements and DFD
questions.text: Scenario 1. A student wants to develop a mobile app for schoolteachers that would allow them to keep track of records of the classroom learning achievements and their homework reports. The teachers currently manage these records manually and want to transition to a more efficient and automated system. The teachers should be able to add and delete students from the app, assign homework to classes and present the records of results to the students, parents, and school administration in a clear and concise manner, and send those records directly to students and parents.

parts.title: System requirements and DFD (a)
parts.text:
State three system requirements for the mobile app considering the needs of the schoolteachers in Scenario 1.

For example: the app should contain a communication feature for sending updates or announcements.

scheme.mark_scheme:
• Ability to delete students’ records (1)
• Ability to add students’ records (1)
• To track homework/progress (1)
• To report results to students/parents/administrators (1)
• To assign homework tasks (1)

[max 3]

Accept requirements related to the scenario
scheme.model_answer:
1. Ability to add students’ records.
2. Ability to delete students’ records.
3. To track homework/progress.
scheme.ai_instructions: Accept requirements related to the scenario. Do not award the printed example as one of the three answers unless used with a distinct relevant feature not already credited.

parts.title: System requirements and DFD (b)
parts.text:

Name two elements that should be described in a data dictionary.

validations (1)

key field (1)

scheme.model_answer:

scheme.ai_instructions: Award any two distinct elements from the mark scheme, maximum 2 marks.

parts.title: System requirements and DFD (c)(i)
parts.text:
Scenario 2. An online store of goods accepts orders through calls. An order includes the following data: customer information and information about ordered goods.

When placing an order, it is required that:
– the system checks if a client exists in the database, and if not, then the details of the client are added to the database
– the order is placed in the system
– during the checkout process customers’ details in the database can be edited. When placing orders, the manager can read and record information about current orders.

Create Level 0 DFD (Data Flow Diagram).

scheme.mark_scheme:
entity (1)

processes (both 1 and 2) (1)

data storage (both clients and orders) (1)

data flow (3 of 7 are correct) (1)

data flow (all 7 are correct) (1)

[5]
scheme.model_answer: A Level 0 DFD with an external entity for the client/customer call, two processes for checking/entering clients and making/recording orders, data stores for list of clients and list of orders, and seven appropriate labelled data flows for order information, client information, client confirmation, order information for orders, product information, and order detail.
scheme.ai_instructions: Award marks for a valid Level 0 DFD using standard DFD conventions. Credit equivalent labels if the flows and stores match the scenario.

parts.title: System requirements and DFD (c)(ii)
parts.text: Explain the purpose of DFD in system development.

scheme.mark_scheme:
a graphical representation of how data moves/transfers between processes (1)

the processes or functions within the system (1)

data storage in a system (1)

a holistic view / understanding of the entire software system / architecture (1)

[Max 2]

points.criterion: a graphical representation of how data moves/transfers between processes
the processes or functions within the system
a holistic view / understanding of the entire software system / architecture

scheme.model_answer: A DFD gives a graphical representation of how data moves between processes, functions and data storage in a system, helping developers understand the whole system architecture.
scheme.ai_instructions: Award any two relevant points from the mark scheme, maximum 2 marks.

questions.title: Relational database and SQL
questions.text:
Scenario 3. An information system of a school has a relational database STUDENT_DB. The database has three tables to store students’ details, details of the course, and details of the teachers.

The structure of the database is shown below:

```
student_tbl(StudentID, FirstName, SecondName, Grade, DateofBirth)
course_tbl(StudentID, CourseID, Classroom)
courseteacher_tbl(CourseID, CourseName, TeacherName)
```

The following table shows records of the student_tbl table.

| StudentID | FirstName | SecondName | Grade | DateofBirth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 001 | Sarsen | Dostayev | 10 | 23/10/2007 |
| 002 | Aiman | Armanova | 9 | 10/05/2008 |
| 003 | Polina | Sergeyeva | 10 | 04/03/2007 |

record

parts.title: Relational database and SQL (c)
parts.text: State the difference between simple and composite primary keys.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Simple primary keys use a single field… (1)

… Composite primary keys use multiple fields (1)

Composite primary keys use multiple fields

parts.title: Relational database and SQL (d)

parts.title: Relational database and SQL (f)
parts.text: Describe the type of relationship between tables student_tbl and course_tbl.

scheme.mark_scheme:
student_tbl table (has primary key- StudentID) will link to foreign key StudentID (in the course_tbl table) (1)

relation will be one-to-many (1)

[2]

points.criterion: student_tbl table (has primary key- StudentID) will link to foreign key StudentID (in the course_tbl table)

questions.title: Product Price Calculator app
questions.text:
Scenario 4. A food store buys products and aims to sell the goods at a profit. The food store ordered a Product Price Calculator app to calculate the selling price of the goods.

The app will record the following data: the product code (contains letters and numbers), the product name, the price paid, and the date of the product order.

The selling price is calculated as follows: if the initial price is less than 1000 tenge, the selling price should be equal to the initial price increased by 30%, otherwise, the selling price should be equal to the initial price increased by 15%.

By the end of the day, the total profit from the sale of products is calculated.

parts.title: Product Price Calculator app (a)
parts.text: Draw a flowchart of the Product Price Calculator app using a loop structure.

scheme.mark_scheme:
condition (1)

loop (1)

input (1)

output (1)

process (1)

[5]
scheme.model_answer: A flowchart that inputs product code, name, price paid and order date, uses a loop to process products, tests whether price < 1000, calculates selling price as price*1.3 or price*1.15, calculates profit/total profit and outputs the results.
scheme.ai_instructions: Award marks for correct flowchart components matching the scenario. Credit any valid loop structure.

element to output the selling price (1)

element to output total profit (1)

labels on components (1)

[7]

points.criterion: 4 input elements (product code, name, price paid, order date)
element to output the selling price

scheme.model_answer: A labelled Product Price Calculator app interface with input fields for product code, product name, price paid and order date; a Product Category drop-down list; a Best Sale Product checkbox; a Calculate/Submit button; and output areas for selling price and total profit.
scheme.ai_instructions: Award for components present and labelled. Layout does not need to match the example exactly.

parts.title: Boolean logic and truth table (a)(i)
parts.text:
Draw the Logic Circuit Diagram for the given Boolean expression.

Q = (A + B)′ + A * (A′ + B′)

scheme.mark_scheme:
correct use of NOR gate (3) (1)

correct use of OR gate (4, 6) (1)

correct use of AND gate (5) (1)

correct use of NOT gate (1, 2) (1)

[4]
scheme.model_answer: A logic circuit for Q = (A + B)′ + A * (A′ + B′): A and B feed a NOR gate; A and B also feed NOT gates, whose outputs feed an OR gate; the OR gate output is ANDed with A; the NOR output and AND output feed a final OR gate to produce Q.

accepted.expression: NOT (A OR B) OR (A AND ((NOT A) OR (NOT B)))

scheme.ai_instructions: Award gate-use marks as specified. Equivalent layouts are acceptable if the expression is implemented correctly.

parts.title: Boolean logic and truth table (a)(ii)
parts.text: Simplify the logic expression.

scheme.mark_scheme:
correct use of De Morgan’s law (1)

correct use of identity law (1)

correct use of complement law (1)

correct use of multiplication law (1)

Solution:

Q = (A + B)′ + A * (A′ + B′)
= A′ * B′ + A * A′ + A * B′
= A′ * B′ + 0 + A * B′
= B′ * (A′ + A)
= B′ * 1
= B′

[4]

points.criterion: correct use of De Morgan’s law

scheme.ai_instructions: This is a simplify/show-working question and must be graded by reasoning. Award marks for the correct laws used and valid simplification steps; the final simplified expression is B′.
